summaryZh: Kleinfeld 团队研究脑回路设计与功能的原理，涉及感觉编码、运动控制和脑血管调节。团队使用啮齿动物实验，结合解剖、连接组学、电与光生理、成像及计算分析。
researchQuestions: 在血管运输特性波动和代谢需求变化时，脑如何保持可靠的血液灌注？

evidence.quote: Neurophysics Research ( Turn and face the strange *) Philosophy: We seek to discover principles that explain the design and function of circuits in the brain. Our experiments involve rodents. Our work is guided by curiosity, theory, and Newton's well quoted missive that " Truth is ever to be found in the simplicity, and not in the multiplicity and confusion of things ." Yet despite our enthusiasm, planning, and persistence, we approach problems with eyes wide open, tempered by Feyman's remark that " Reality is under no obligation to make sense to us. There's a genuine mystery baked into the structure of things and no amount of clever equation writing will dissolve it completely ." Active sensing: Our goal is an integrated circuit of sensory encoding and movement. Specifically, we addresses the circuits for orofacial motor actions that underlie exploration and foraging. These circuits coordinate movement of sensory organs and sensors and then compute a stable world view in the presence of self-motion. Our current focus is three-fold: brainstem connections for the modulation of orofacial and head movement by the breathing oscillator; midbrain feedback to refine the coordination of concurrent orofacial motor actions; and thalamocortical to cortical transformations specifically to deduce egocentric object location through vibrissa touch as a basis for combining sensory inputs. We use a full spectrum of approaches that include anatomy, behavior, computational analysis, electro- and opto-physiology, and structural and functional imaging. Brain vasodynamics: Our goal is an integrated view of how the brain is reliably perfused with blood in the face of fluctuations in vascular transport properties and shifting metabolic needs. We address vascular control in terms of the known vascular connectome and feedback dynamics and, for the case of vasomotion, are guided by the mathematics of coupled oscillators. Our current focus is three-fold: exploring and formulating the spatiotemporal dynamics of arteriole vaso-oscillations in terms of competive inputs from internal brain signals and external sensation; measuring and understanding metabolic loads at the level of individual brain cells; and using graph-theoretic analysis of the brain vascular connectome to determine the self-and cross-influence of flow through the vascular network. We use a full spectrum of approaches that include anatomy, connectomics, analytical and computational analysis, electro- and opto-physiology, and structural and functional imaging. Neurotechnology and analysis: We maintain an ongoing effort to develop tools that advance our scientific studies. Our past efforts involve functional imaging, e.g., adaptive-optics, the automation of anatomical studies, e.g., all-optical histology, and analytical methods to model and understand neural circuits. We are presently exploring mixed genetic and optical means to image within dense brainstem networks. We maintain electronic, optical, chemical, and computational workshops and have access to classic and additive mechanical shops.
